# Cluster 16: Leg compliance design

2 papers · years 2019–2020 · 2 curated

## Top authors

- AhmadSharbafi (1)
- Sharbafi (1)

## Pathways represented

- Biomechanically mediated preflexive feedback (1)

## Key papers (by citations)

- **AhmadSharbafi 2020** — [Parallel compliance design for increasing robustness and efficiency in legged locomotion - theoretical backgro](https://doi.org/10.1109/tmech.2020.3019686)  
  - Extends concurrent design of walking controllers and parallel mechanical compliance (EHPC with fewer assumptions; CPC generalized beyond hybrid zero dynamics) with Lyapunov, boundedness, and input-to-state-stability robustness analysis, a step-by-step compass-gait design with MATLAB code, and hopper-robot experiments using pneumatic artificial muscles as tunable parallel compliance - a systematic route to co-designing actuator compliance and control for robust, efficient legged locomotion.  
  - *Robot/sim:* Co-design parallel compliance (e.g., pneumatic artificial muscles acting as tunable springs alongside the controller) with the walking controller using the EHPC/CPC procedure on a compass-gait model, and quantify robustness and energy gains versus controller-only designs.
- **Sharbafi 2019** — [Parallel Compliance Design for Increasing Robustness and Efficiency in Legged Locomotion—Proof of Concept](https://doi.org/10.1109/tmech.2019.2917416)  
  - pathways: Biomechanically mediated preflexive feedback  
  - A hybrid-zero-dynamics co-design methodology for parallel joint compliance and control shows passive parallel elastic elements robustify bipedal walking against model uncertainty (ground slope, segment lengths) while cutting torque demand, with pneumatic artificial muscles proposed as the physical parallel-compliance element, preflexive mechanics substituting for sensor-driven controller adaptation.  
  - *Robot/sim:* Co-design parallel joint springs with the controller using hybrid zero dynamics; sweep compliance under ground-slope and segment-length uncertainty and compare torque cost and robustness against a no-compliance baseline, modeling the springs with pneumatic-muscle force-length behavior.
